input: head is null or a list head; x is an exact integer threshold in the same paired numeric domain as node values. Each nonempty input is a finite, acyclic singly linked list of caller-supplied nodes with ordinary data fields val and next. val contains JavaScript Number integers, excluding BigInt; next is another node or null. next fields are writable and nodes within a list are distinct. Accessors, proxies, custom attribute behavior, concurrent observation or mutation during the call, and malformed links are outside the domain. Inputs must fit both runtimes. External caller references to individual nodes are allowed. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: The head of a stable partition of the original nodes: all nodes with val < x, followed by all nodes with val >= x, preserving original relative order within both groups. Every original node occurs exactly once. An empty input returns null; all-below and all-at-least inputs retain their original node order and head.
mutation_aliasing: Detaches each original node by setting next to null before appending it to one of two local chains, then joins the lower chain to the upper chain. Only original next fields change; values and all other fields are unchanged. No node is cloned, dropped or replaced. Each original node appears exactly once in the acyclic output, whose tail next is null. Caller-held aliases observe the final partitioned next graph; the caller's head reference binding itself is not reassigned. The two local sentinels are never returned or linked from any input node. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The paired domain restricts node values and x to exact integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991], excluding booleans, negative zero, NaN, infinities and BigInt. Python uses plain int and JavaScript uses Number. Values are compared only, never modified or used in arithmetic, so Python and JavaScript comparisons agree on this domain. No list-length counter, bitwise coercion or recursion depth is used.
complexity: O(n + 1) time and O(1) auxiliary space for n input nodes. Each node is visited once and appended to exactly one chain; joining the chains is O(1). Both sentinel instances and all borrowed references are charged. There is no recursion, collection of node references, node copying or value arithmetic. Field access, reference assignment and bounded-integer comparison are constant cost.

helpers.name: Link
helpers.contract: A local sentinel-only class whose constructor stores the supplied next_node reference, defaulting to null, in its sole instance data field next. It does not read, copy or construct caller ListNode objects and has no val field. Sentinels never become nodes in the returned list.
helpers.cost: Two constructor calls allocate two sentinel objects, each in O(1) time and O(1) space. The complete 80-byte UTF-8 helper definition, from class Link through its final definition newline, is byte-identical in 0021.js, 0024.js and 0086.js, and is fully charged in every standalone candidate. Separator newlines are charged in total source bytes.

source_accounting: The complete standalone candidate is 756 UTF-8 bytes, including the 80-byte Link helper, input-shape comment, separator newlines, Solution wrapper, method, constructor calls and terminal newline. Caller ListNode is an explicit input shape, not an uncharged dummy-node constructor: all allocated sentinels use the fully included Link implementation. Shared helper spelling is not a free library. There are no imports, generated source or hidden expansion. Any eventual judge adapter is additional charged source.
evidence_boundary: Independently authored dev_fit candidate outside frozen source sets. No candidate execution, predecessor equivalence, behavioral qualification, benchmark acceptance or M1 progress is claimed. The mandatory isolated judge is unavailable; AST parsing, JavaScript syntax and metadata checks do not establish runtime correctness. Independent source-bound qualification must compare value order, mapped original node identities and the complete post-call next graph, including caller aliases and terminal null links, not just serialized values. Empty, singleton, duplicate-value and odd/even-length inputs plus declared ordering boundaries require qualification before promotion.
